subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Which WebChat client metadata may agents see, and should it be derived only from validated Gateway connect identity or also include untrusted browser/app hints?
rationale: The remaining work crosses from diagnostic connection metadata into agent-visible context that can influence behavior, so automation should not choose the trust model or permanent API shape.

options.title: Expose trusted Gateway identity only
options.body: Add a typed agent-facing field derived from validated Gateway client id, mode, and platform, while keeping ad hoc hints out of agent authority.

options.title: Allow explicitly untrusted hints
options.body: Expose browser or app hints only when clearly marked diagnostic and untrusted, accepting more API complexity for flexibility.

options.title: Keep identity diagnostic-only
options.body: Leave client identity in Gateway connection state and logs until maintainers approve a stronger agent-facing use case.

recommendation.title: Expose trusted Gateway identity only
recommendation.body: Add a typed agent-facing field derived from validated Gateway client id, mode, and platform, while keeping ad hoc hints out of agent authority.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is primarily the Gateway auth/security trust boundary for client metadata.
